passages.provision_quote: An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision.
passages.note: Mandatory notice-and-restriction scheme with enforcement shows more oversight than optional guidelines but does not match the safety-testing, developer-liability, or government-approval clauses of any single rung.
passages.actor_quote: Introduced by Senator McNerney (Coauthors: Assembly Members Bryan and Elhawary)

rows.reasoning: McNerney authored SB 7 (2025-2026), which requires employer notice of automated decision systems and provides that "An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision," enforced by Labor Commissioner civil penalties. This shows more oversight than "Suggest AI safety guidelines but let companies choose whether to follow them," but its notice-and-restriction scheme does not match "Require safety testing before AI can be used in high-stakes areas like hiring, healthcare, and policing" or "Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm," since liability here falls on employers for process violations rather than developers for harm caused.
